statement: (i) Find $\\int e^{-x}\\sin x\\,dx$. (ii) Verify your answer by differentiation.
solution: (i) Let $I=\\int e^{-x}\\sin x\\,dx$. By parts twice (or using the standard formula $\\int e^{ax}\\sin bx\\,dx=e^{ax}(a\\sin bx-b\\cos bx)/(a^{2}+b^{2})$): with $a=-1,b=1$, $I=-\\frac{e^{-x}}{2}(\\sin x+\\cos x)+C$. (ii) Differentiating $-\\frac{e^{-x}}{2}(\\sin x+\\cos x)$: $-\\frac{1}{2}[-e^{-x}(\\sin x+\\cos x)+e^{-x}(\\cos x-\\sin x)]=e^{-x}\\sin x$. Verified.
